newsitem.title: USA: Kmart to start system-wide cash card usage.
newsitem.headline: Kmart to start system-wide cash card usage.

text.p: Kmart Corp. is introducing a Kmart Cash Card later this month that will replace gift certificates and some cash refunds, and can also be used as an AT&T Corp. calling card.

While other retailers offer the so-called stored-value cards for some transactions, Troy, Mich.-based Kmart is believed to be the first mass retailer to offer a card for so many different transactions, said Tom Recktenwald, an executive vice president at Louisville, Ky.-based Stored Value Systems, which is administering the card programme for Kmart.

Kmart will use the cards, which can store any amount of cash value, to replace of gift certificates. For returns made without a receipt, the store can enter credit into the cards instead of giving customers cash.

When a customer uses the card, it is swiped through a Kmart cash register, like a credit card or debit card with a magnetic stripe. The card is "read" and the value of the purchase is deducted. A customer may "re-load" the card at any Kmart register.

Aside from making shopping easier for some customers, Kmart also expects the cards to save the retailer money in terms of paperwork, while also minimising abuses in its cash refund process, said Robert Burton, Kmart chief finacial officer.
"We're doing this because we think this saves us dollars, in addition to providing a benefit to the customer," Burton said.
Kmart's stock fell 44 cents to $11.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
